summary: BLM lookout in Klamath County: first house built 1964, burned in the July 1979 Bryant Fire, rebuilt 1980-81, transferred to the landowner in 2007.

facts.design: BLM flat-top cab on a 30-foot open tower; the register and firelookout.com say timber, Peakbagging says steel

access.note: stands on private land since the 2007 transfer; Peakbagging reports the access road in bad shape in 2017

visit.trail_note: road in bad shape and would need major repairs before it could be used (Peakbagging, photo of July 2, 2017); on private land

events.note: first structure on the summit, a two-story enclosed lookout house built by the BLM; a December 1963 announcement had called for a lookout building the next year
site went into service as a National Climatic Data Center weather station
the weather station closed on October 31, 1976
Bryant Fire discovered July 17, 1979 about 25 miles southeast of Klamath Falls; reported at nearly 10,000 acres by July 20; the source marks its date as approximate
fire destroyed the first lookout; a newspaper quoted by oregonlookouts says so, and firelookout.com and Peakbagging agree

replacement 30-foot tower; the register gives 1981, firelookout.com and Peakbagging give 1980 for construction; built by Johnson Construction of Klamath Falls for about $90,000; back in operation by July 1981
new tower stands about 50 yards from the old tower site, on Loveness Timber Co. property
lookout moved into the tower in June 1981 and was expected to leave in early October
structure declared surplus and transferred to the landowner as is, where is
National Historic Lookout Register registration date June 22, 2022

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register gives 1981 as the build year, firelookout.com and Peakbagging give 1980 for the new tower's construction, and a July 1981 newspaper says it was back in operation after about a year of work. The story reports 1980 as construction and 1981 as return to service. The first summit structure dates to 1964 and is a separate build.

notes_for_editor: Height 9.1 m is the 30-foot tower, not the elevation (brief's 1968.7 m is elevation). Unresolved: timber (NHLR, firelookout.com) vs steel (Peakbagging) for the 1980-81 tower. Newest condition evidence is a July 2, 2017 photo; no later source checked. No rental found. The lessons.wildfire.gov page covers the same 1979 fire (a 20-person crew deployed shelters) but does not name this lookout; it marks its date approximate and was not used for crew details. Brief's 1981 build year is kept. Access set to private from the NHLR 'Private Land' field and Peakbagging.
